paper.title: Sun-like stars show lowered X-ray activity together with over-rotation at beyond-solar ages
paper.abstract: In recent years, substructure in the age-rotation relationship of cool, sun-like stars has been identified, showing deviations from the historical Skumanich law. Since magnetic activity is expected to be the physical root cause of the stellar spin-down, namely via the magnetic braking process mediated through stellar winds, changes in spin-down should correspond to unusual activity behaviour. We selected a sample of old sun-like stars in the solar neighborhood with asteroseismic age estimates and measured rotation periods, and present an analysis of their magnetic activity using deep X-ray observations from XMM-Newton. We observe that sample stars less massive than the Sun (late-G and early-K) agree well with the established rotation-activity relationship, while early-G and late-F stars with masses above solar tend to be unusually X-ray dim for their rotation period. The latter stars rotate faster than same-colour stars in the solar-age open cluster M67, despite being older than M67. Those stars are characterized by either low metallicity ([Fe/H]$\approx -0.2$ dex compared to solar) or by a mix of low coronal temperatures ($< 1.5$ million K) and very low X-ray surface fluxes ($\lesssim 10^4$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$). We conclude that there is sufficient dynamo activity for coronal emission in the sample stars, since we successfully detect the majority of them in our X-ray observations. We argue that stars with extremely low coronal temperature and/or low X-ray flux through the stellar surface may produce an inefficient spin-down through hampered angular momentum shedding. If this is indeed the cause for their over-rotation, the onset age of this effect would need to be at an age of approximately 3~Gyr. However, this behaviour is at odds with studies of stars in the open cluster M67 with a cluster age of $\sim4$ Gyr, which do not show a faster-rotating population of sun-like stars.

paper.title: Neural-Network Identification of LIGO Noise Transients Using Binary Auxiliary-Channel Activity
paper.abstract: Transient noise artifacts ("glitches") in the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO), Virgo and KAGRA (LVK) detectors can mimic astrophysical signals and reduce confidence in gravitational-wave detections. The LVK's iDQ pipeline identifies these glitches by analyzing correlations between auxiliary sensors and the strain channel using the Ordered Veto List (OVL) algorithm. We revisit neural-network approaches to this problem using modern training infrastructure and introduce two architectures: GIANTS, a single network trained on all auxiliary-channel features, and TITAN, a mixture-of-experts model composed of subsystem-specific networks and a learned combiner. Evaluated on ten independent test periods spanning LIGO's third observing run, both models outperform OVL on most test sets, with TITAN providing the most consistent performance over time. We further show that nearly all predictive information contained in Omicron trigger features is captured by a simple binary indicator of auxiliary-channel activity. Networks trained on these binary inputs achieve essentially the same performance as models using the full 8,440-dimensional feature set while reducing the input dimensionality by an order of magnitude. These results demonstrate that modern neural networks provide a robust alternative to OVL and suggest that substantially simpler data representations are sufficient for accurate glitch identification in future iDQ deployments.

paper.title: Boundary preparation and anomalous relaxation near a black hole exceptional point
paper.abstract: We study the relaxation of a Robin scalar field near a stable exceptional point of a planar Schwarzschild AdS black hole, where finite boundary driving controls the recovery time without changing the leading decay rate at linear order. At the exceptional point, two weighted moments of the source determine the time dependence of the leading response. When the zeroth moment vanishes while the first remains nonzero, the linear time factor is eliminated, leaving an ordinary exponential decay. With suitable boundary preparation, a perturbation that retains more energy at release can nevertheless reach a common recovery threshold sooner. At the exceptional point, its recovery time advantage over a fixed reference that retains the linear factor grows as $γ_*^{-1}\log\log(1/θ)$ as the common amplitude threshold $θ$ approaches zero, where $γ_*$ is the common decay rate. The source moments also determine the constant term in this asymptotic time difference. Full scalar field evolution on a fixed background near the exceptional point illustrates the reversal for pulses matched in duration, boundary task, source cost, and injected work, within the time window where the small spectral splitting remains unresolved. The injected work also modifies the final spectrum through gravitational heating. When weak driving begins with a black hole at the exceptional point, the temperature rise is quadratic in the source amplitude, whereas the final pole splitting is linear in its magnitude. This splitting limits the time window over which the exceptional point recovery law can be observed.

paper.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
paper.abstract: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this Hamiltonian from the equations of motion alone, show why the orbit average gives the correct equations, and relate its constants of motion to those of the full system. We then construct the action-angle variables and frequencies with the recently introduced method of fictitious variables, and propose a criterion for the breakdown of the integrability conditions. This criterion recovers the separatrices of simple classical systems and the up-down instability, whose thresholds we give explicitly for eccentric orbits. We also show that, when all binaries of an ensemble share the same parameters and radiation reaction does not depend on the spins, the Hamiltonian structure preserves an isotropic distribution of spin directions. We confirm numerically that isotropy can be lost when the parameters are correlated with the spin directions. Finally, we use the orbit-averaged Hamiltonian to generalize the projected effective spin to binary neutron stars, for which it is not conserved, and obtain a closed form valid for eccentric orbits.

paper.title: Electro-Penrose Process in Charged BTZ Black Holes: From Probe Limit to Thermodynamic Backreaction
paper.abstract: We investigate the electro-Penrose process (EPP) in $(2+1)$-dimensional charged Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ) spacetime, from probe-limit particle dynamics to quasistatic thermodynamic backreaction. In the probe background, neutral particles have no exterior circular orbits, and charged circular motion requires a minimum repulsive coupling. We derive the maximum single-event energy at fixed decay data, including fragment masses and charge allocation, and check capture and collection at a finite receiver in anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. Repetitive radial extraction on successive exact stationary backgrounds uses an adaptive incident specific charge. The continuum mass-charge path identifies the switch between incident turning-point and negative-energy stopping, supported by numerical checks. The prescribed sequences terminate at nonzero residual charge before exhausting the energy reservoir, providing a protocol-dependent third-law analogy. The consumed reservoir is divided between extracted energy and irreversible growth of irreducible mass, with proportions depending on the protocol.

paper.title: Welopō'ai: A peculiar triple system 8 pc from the Sun
paper.abstract: Context. We report the serendipitous discovery of a white dwarf companion to the M4 V dwarf Welopo'ai Aa (IRAS 21500+5903) during a radial-velocity search for exoplanets with SPIRou. The system is located at 8.46 pc and forms a hierarchical triple with a more distant white dwarf, which has no known analogue within 30 pc. Aims. We characterise the orbital architecture and component masses through a joint Keplerian fit of radial velocities and astrometry, derive the physical parameters of the M dwarf and both white dwarfs, and discuss the implications for common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple dynamics. Methods. We obtained radial velocity measurements with SPIRou spread over 4.8 yr, revealing a large-amplitude signal ($\sim$16 km/s peak-to-peak) that is inconsistent with planetary companions. Follow-up speckle imaging with 'Alopeke at Gemini North and near-infrared (NIR) imaging with GNIRS confirmed a white dwarf companion at sub-arcsecond separation. Results. The system comprises an inner binary with a semi-major axis of $4.644 \pm 0.017$ au ($P \approx 9.83$ yr), consisting of the primary M4 V ($M = 0.4189^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072} M_\odot$) and a white dwarf companion ($M = 0.6180^{+0.0046}_{-0.0045} M_\odot$, $T_{\rm eff} \sim 5210 \pm 320$ K, cooling age 5.3-5.5 Gyr). This inner pair lies at a projected separation of 123.9 au ($P > 1000$ yr) from a previously known white dwarf. The dynamically determined mass of the inner white dwarf is one of only a handful of such measurements for white dwarfs within 20 pc, and the most precise, at the sub-percent (0.7%) level. Conclusions. This system is the closest known triple containing multiple white dwarfs and offers direct dynamical constraints on common-envelope evolution and hierarchical triple stability. Furthermore, a tentative near-infrared (IR) excess towards the inner white dwarf further hints at circumstellar dust.

paper.title: Interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimation for fast radio burst cosmology
paper.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe the integrated free-electron density along extragalactic sightlines and can be used to study late-time cosmic evolution. Conventional Bayesian analyses require repeated evaluations of computationally expensive likelihoods, making inference increasingly challenging as FRB catalogs grow. In this work, we develop an interpretable attention-based neural posterior estimator (AttNPE) for rapid posterior inference of the physical parameters from FRB catalogs with measured redshifts. The attention encoder compresses the catalog into a low-dimensional representation, and a conditional masked autoregressive flow maps samples from a base distribution to the seven-dimensional posterior. AttNPE yields posterior distributions in close agreement with Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), recovering the parameter correlations in both simulated and observed FRB catalogs. For the observed catalog, AttNPE generates $5\times10^4$ posterior samples in $0.036$~s after training, compared with $72.8$~h for the reference MCMC run, giving an elapsed-time ratio of $O(10^6)$. The attention-weight analysis shows that intermediate-redshift FRBs ($0.3\leq z<0.7$) account for the largest share of the total attention averaged over simulated catalogs following the observed redshift distribution, consistent with the combined influence of source abundance and redshift-dependent sensitivity. These results demonstrate the potential of interpretable neural posterior estimation for efficient and repeated inference in FRB cosmology.

paper.title: Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with mass estimates verifiable in Gaia Data Release 4
paper.abstract: Gaia Science Alerts provide an all-sky stream of photometric transients, including events consistent with gravitational microlensing. For such events, forthcoming epoch astrometry from the Gaia mission offers the possibility of testing photometric lens mass predictions. While microlensing parallax inferred from the photometric light curve can constrain the event geometry, a direct lens mass measurement additionally requires the angular Einstein radius, which may be accessible through astrometric microlensing. We aim to construct a pre-Data-Release-4 (DR4) sample of Gaia microlensing events for which the available photometry provides a measurable microlensing-parallax signal. This allows us to derive statistical predictions for the lens mass and distance. We forward-modelled these events to predict the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal in Gaia DR4. We identify 56 Gaia Science Alerts microlensing events with 71 point-source point-lens solutions with annual parallaxes that satisfy our fit-quality, posterior-boundedness, and parallax-significance criteria. Lens masses and distances were inferred using two prior-based frameworks, pyLIMASS and the Besançon Galaxy Model, which combine the measured microlensing parameters and Gaia source information with stellar-population and Galactic models. These inferred parameters were used to simulate Gaia DR4-like along-scan astrometry and estimate the detectability of the astrometric microlensing signal. The inferred lens masses and distances remain strongly prior-dependent without a direct angular Einstein radius measurement. Among the 284 event-solution-prior branches, 47 are classified as high-confidence astrometric detections using Gaia DR4-like simulations. These predictions can be tested once epoch astrometry is released in Gaia DR4.

paper.title: A high-resolution search for axion dark-matter flows with ORGAN-Q
paper.abstract: We search for narrow axion dark-matter flows using the high-resolution data acquired during the ORGAN-Q experiment. The analysis covers nine potential axion linewidths from 0.466$~$Hz to 119.209$~$Hz, equivalent to axion effective quality factors $1.3\times 10^{10}$ to $5.2\times 10^7$, over the range 6.1550$~$GHz to 6.3496$~$GHz, corresponding to axion masses of approximately 25.455$~μ\mathrm{eV}$ to 26.260$~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Once contributions from native-bin correlations, data-quality and interference vetoes, frequency-dependent system noise, the cavity response, and filter attenuation are accounted for, no candidate satisfies the required persistence ratio in any search bandwidth. Across the nine assumed linewidths, the strongest $95\%$ KSVZ axion-flow density limits range from 22.8$~\mathrm{GeVcm^{-3}}$ for a $0.466~\mathrm{Hz}$ signal to $153.7~\mathrm{GeVcm}^{-3}$ for a $119.209~\mathrm{Hz}$ signal, with both attained near $m_a=25.857~μ\mathrm{eV}$.

paper.title: Cosmological First-Order Phase Transitions with Full Nonlinear Gravity
paper.abstract: Cosmological first-order phase transitions can contribute to the stochastic gravitational wave background. For decades, these first-order phase transitions have been studied using a Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker background where the gravitational waves are treated as linear perturbations. Here, we present simulations of a first-order phase transition in the presence of fully nonlinear general relativity, using the BSSN formalism. We simulate a universe that contains a scalar field alongside a relativistic radiation fluid. We focus on GUT-scale transitions in which bubbles nucleate near the horizon size. We describe a method to construct initial data that satisfies the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints, starting from a Coleman--de~Luccia-like bubble profile and adjusting the bubble radius. We compute the gravitational wave spectrum directly from the trace-free extrinsic curvature and find a present-day peak amplitude of $Ω_{\rm GW,0}h^2 \sim 5\times 10^{-11}$, consistent with earlier results that do not include nonlinear gravity. The peak frequency depends on the symmetry-breaking scale and could fall anywhere from the LISA band to GHz frequencies. At late times, the field fragments into long-lived oscillons, which push its effective equation of state toward that of matter.

paper.title: The infrared arc around $α$ Crucis: a weak interaction with a structured interstellar medium
paper.abstract: Infrared arc-shaped structures around early-type stars are commonly interpreted as stellar wind bow shocks, although their morphology may also be shaped by gas motions and density variations in the surrounding interstellar medium. We present a multiwavelength study of the infrared arc associated with the nearby $α$ Crucis system, comprising HD 108248 (B0.5 IV), HD 108249 (B1 V), and HD 108250 (B4 V). We combine WISE, Herschel, Planck, stellar astrometry, and eROSITA X-ray data to investigate the structure and its relation to the stellar components. The WISE W4 ridge extends over $\sim$0.65 pc and has a median PSF-corrected width of $\sim$0.037 pc. The HD 108248/HD 108249 pair lies $\sim$0.13 pc from the ridge, compared with $\sim$0.17 pc for HD 108250. Relative to the mean motion of the Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) subgroup of the Scorpius-Centaurus association, the close pair is consistent with LCC, whereas HD 108250 has a transverse peculiar velocity of only $\sim$1.8 km s$^{-1}$. Its motion lies within $\sim$23$^\circ$ of the geometrical symmetry axis of the infrared arc, but points in the opposite sense from the arc. Herschel maps show slightly higher median dust temperature ($ΔT_d\sim$0.8 K) and molecular-hydrogen column density ($ΔN_{\rm H2}\sim$7$\times$10$^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$) toward the W4-defined region than in the nearby background. On larger scales, Planck maps reveal a strongly structured microwave environment around the system. Both the HD 108248/HD 108249 pair and HD 108250 are detected by eROSITA, with the former approximately 60 times more luminous in X-rays. The combined morphology, kinematics, and dust properties do not support an unambiguous classical high-velocity bow-shock interpretation. Instead, the arc likely traces a weak interaction between the multiple stellar system and an inhomogeneous ambient medium.

paper.title: A twist in the tail: GWLENS, a fast and accurate tool for wave-optics lensing of gravitational waves
paper.abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime requires evaluating the Fresnel--Kirchhoff diffraction integral, whose integrand is highly oscillatory and must be evaluated numerically, as closed-form solutions exist only for a few lens models. We present a novel, efficient algorithm that splits the integration domain at a point beyond the region containing the lensed images. The bounded head region is integrated along the real axis with Gauss--Legendre quadrature, while the semi-infinite tail is rotated into the complex plane, where the integrand decays exponentially, and is evaluated with Gauss--Laguerre quadrature. Since the image region is never deformed, the method avoids the treatment of poles and branch cuts required by existing contour-deformation approaches. Our results agree with the exact point-mass solution to $10^{-13}$ and show good agreement with other methods. We present several examples for non-trivial lens models, showing potential for parameter estimation of realistic lenses. The method is particularly efficient when the amplification factor is needed for many source positions. In addition to transient broadband compact binary coalescence GW signals, we apply it to long-duration (continuous), quasi-monochromatic GW signals, for which the relative motion of source and lens makes the amplification factor time-dependent over the observation. The implementation is publicly available in the Python package GWLENS.

paper.title: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic constraints on first-order phase transitions: A tale of priors
paper.abstract: We re-examine the methodology for constraining cosmological first-order phase transitions from gravitational-wave searches using Bayesian statistical analysis. Specifically, we use results from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA searches for a stochastic gravitational wave background during observing runs O1--O4a. We explore multiple prior choices across three categories of fit parameters: geometrical parameters, thermodynamical parameters of phase transitions, and the parameters of an Abelian Higgs particle physics model. Our key finding is that the constraints on most parameters describing gravitational waves from a phase transition depend strongly on the prior. Consequently, the data do not yet allow to derive robust constraints on these parameters. Besides, even if a parameter is meaningfully constrained, the upper limit can vary significantly with the prior range. We provide practical recommendations for assessing the robustness of parameter estimates and guidelines for rigorously testing prior independence in future analyses.

paper.title: Early spectra of AT2017gfo from scaled 3D merger ejecta: mass--velocity distribution, 3D structure, and treatment of line opacity
paper.abstract: We present ARTIS radiative transfer calculations for neutron star merger ejecta with line-by-line opacities, wavelength-calibrated lanthanide data, and time-dependent r-process compositions and thermalisation, testing how the early kilonova depends on the mass-velocity distribution, dimensionality, and line treatment. We rescale 3D dynamical ejecta from a merger simulation in density and velocity to approximate AT2017gfo. Mass scaling alone provides good agreement with the bolometric light curve but inconsistent spectra. With velocities additionally halved, the model also reproduces the observed spectra at 1.4, 2.4, and (albeit less accurately) 3.4 days. The Sr II triplet contributes most to the 10500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ peak, and La III and Gd III to the 13500 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ shoulder. Although hydrodynamically not fully self-consistent, this model is to our knowledge the first kilonova model based on calibrated atomic data that reproduces the light curve and main spectral features of the early AT2017gfo, suggesting that total (dynamical plus post-merger) ejecta with higher mass, lower velocity, and similar composition compared to our dynamical ejecta could explain AT2017gfo. A 2D azimuthal average mixes lanthanide-poor with lanthanide-rich regions, smooths the density, and makes the averaged model three times fainter at 1 day and redder throughout than the 3D model, highlighting the importance of 3D modelling. We compare the line-by-line macroatom treatment with expansion-opacity and line-binned schemes with thermal redistribution, using identical atomic data. Luminosities agree to $\lesssim 10$ per cent after 1 day, but the expansion-opacity scheme, unlike converged line-binned schemes, overestimates the spectral flux by up to 20 per cent, which can bias inferred abundances.

paper.title: Stratonovich approximation for halo bias: An efficient framework within excursion set theory
paper.abstract: We develop an efficient framework for calculating halo multiplicity functions and bias parameters in the excursion-set approach based on the previously presented Hertz and Stratonovich approximations for the first-crossing distribution. The framework enables efficient evaluation of first-crossing distributions for a broad class of moving barriers and filter functions, from which halo biases can be calculated within the peak-background split formalism. We compare halo multiplicity functions and biases obtained from these approximations with those computed from first-crossing distributions obtained from numerically generated ensembles of excursion-set trajectories. We find close agreement between predictions based on the Stratonovich approximation and numerical results across a range of barrier parameters and filter choices, demonstrating that the approximation captures the impact of non-Markovian correlations on first-crossing statistics while substantially reducing the computational cost compared to trajectory-based calculations. Overall, this framework provides a flexible and computationally efficient tool for analyzing halo statistics in cosmological applications.

paper.title: Charge at regular centers in curvature-coupled electrodynamics
paper.abstract: An electric or magnetic flux through shrinking symmetry spheres ordinarily produces an $r^{-4}$ Maxwell stress and a singular center. We examine how this obstruction changes when the Maxwell invariant is multiplied by an arbitrary scalar-curvature response $h(R)$. For real, static, spherically symmetric solutions, the difference between the radial and temporal gravitational equations gives a linear equation for a composite response variable. Combined with the trace equation, it bounds the response-weighted Maxwell source whenever the Kretschmann scalar is bounded, without assuming a limit or derivative bounds for the Ricci scalar. Magnetic and electric displacement charges cannot coexist, and neither charge is possible if $h$ remains bounded and bounded away from zero. On either surviving charged branch, the Ricci scalar converges and the weighted source tends to zero. Magnetic charge requires $h=o(r^4)$, whereas electric displacement requires $r^4|h|\to\infty$. Exact solutions show that these thresholds are sharp and realize the $r^6$ magnetic and $r^{-6}$ electric rates for a smooth geometric center. We also classify the zero-response sector, where an electric field may survive even though its displacement charge vanishes.

paper.title: Investigating the Impact of SAX J1808.4-3658's Very Bright Thermonuclear X-ray Burst on the Accretion Disc with NICER
paper.abstract: We analyse a bright thermonuclear X-ray burst from the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar (AMXP) SAX J1808.4-3658, the brightest burst detected by \textit{NICER} to date, to explore interactions between thermonuclear burst radiation and the accretion disc. This burst features a remarkable soft (<1.5 keV) excess in its spectra. For the first time, we simultaneously detect a reflection signal and the signature of an evolving persistent component, with our fits producing a peak persistent scaling factor $f_{a,1} = 59.6\pm0.6$. We find a high peak reflection fraction ($f_{r,1} = 0.82\pm0.15$) and a peak bolometric burst blackbody flux below Eddington (0.68$L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$) despite signatures of photospheric radius expansion. We detect a raised $N_\mathrm{H}$ ($\approx$34% above persistent emission) and raised disc blackbody temperature ($\approx$15% above persistent emission) during the burst's tail. This is the first time that spectroscopic evidence consistent with burst-induced disc heating has been found. We interpret that disc heating could cause the disc to puff up and inhibit burst photons, explaining the high reflection fraction and below-Eddington burst luminosity during the burst peak. We find an increasing count rate starting from $\approx$150s before the burst onset. Spectral analysis revealed a thermal component that evolves towards hotter temperatures closer to the onset of the burst. This is the second detection of this phenomenon from an AMXP. Lastly, we find that both the double-peaked structure and the "pause" in the rise are energy-dependent.

paper.title: Towards modelling redshift uncertainties in the photometric void size function
paper.abstract: We present an extension of the theoretical formalism for the Void Size Function (VSF) to incorporate photometric redshift uncertainties, combining the excursion set with the theory of Lagrangian density peaks. Photometric redshift scatter induces anisotropic line-of-sight smoothing of the density field, which modifies the variance of the field and suppresses the abundance of large voids. We model this effect by damping the variance of the smoothed density field in the theoretical model, and we test it on AbacusSummit halo lightcones with true redshifts and with mock photometric redshifts generated with a Gaussian scatter. The predicted damping of the variance agrees with the one measured in the halo distribution to 1% and the suppression of the VSF due to photometric redshift scatter is well reproduced by the modified model, with recalibrated barrier parameters, for sigma_z <= 0.015 and for voids larger than 40 Mpc/h (about 2.5 mean tracer separations). This work is a first step towards modelling the VSF in modern photometric surveys such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time and the Euclid mission.

paper.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. III. Reissner-Nordstrom spectra from zero to extremal charge
paper.abstract: Earlier calculations left open how gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of charged black holes recover the Schwarzschild spectrum and how the modes near algebraically special frequencies relate to the exact special solutions. We extend our Kerr analysis to Reissner-Nordström black holes by analytically continuing the ingoing horizon solution and locating the zeros of the incoming amplitude at infinity. For each of $\ell=2$ and $3$, we trace the first 42 overtone families from the Schwarzschild limit to extremality. The charge trajectories distinguish crossings of the negative imaginary axis from turns near it and separate the unconventional Schwarzschild modes from neighboring branches. At zero charge the polar algebraically special mode is a QNM. At extremal charge the exact axial special modes are total-transmission modes. Of the 84 families, 75 approach distinct extremal frequencies with finite damping, and nine approach zero frequency with vanishing excitation. At exact extremality we also compute, for the first time, gravitational QNMs on the unconventional Riemann sheet reached across the negative imaginary axis. At intermediate charge, the clearest resonant enhancement of both excitation factors occurs for the $\ell=3$ overtone pairs $(22,23)$ and $(23,24)$.

paper.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
paper.abstract: Fully constraining the neutron star equation of state (EoS) requires combining observations from various channels that probe different density regimes. We perform a joint multimessenger inference of the equation of state using gravitational-wave observations from binary neutron star mergers, NICER mass-radius measurements of X-ray pulsars, and radio timing measurements of massive pulsars. We constrain the parametrized equation of state and perform Bayesian model selection among a set of candidate equations of state. The joint analysis produces a radius of $R_{1.4} = 11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83} \, \rm km$ for a canonical $1.4 \, M_\odot$ neutron star, and a maximum non-rotating neutron star mass of $M_{\rm max} = 2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23} \, M_\odot$ with $90\%$ credible intervals. Gravitational-wave and NICER observations constrain the equation of state at low to intermediate densities, while massive pulsar observations constrain it at high densities by requiring the equation of state to support the neutron star masses. We find no simple correlation between the stiffness of an EoS and Bayesian evidence because the observations probe the pressure at different density regimes. By combining constraints on the equation of state with Bayesian model selection using multimessenger data, our analysis connects macroscopic neutron star measurements to microscopic properties of candidate nuclear matter models.

paper.title: On the cosmic window for neutrino self-interactions
paper.abstract: Neutrino self-interactions ($ν$SI) beyond the Standard Model have arisen as a promising probe of new physics in cosmology. In this Letter, we show that $ν$SI emerging in the low-energy limit of renormalizable theories implies resonant mediator behavior. We identify two regions for $ν$SI: (i) neutrinos become tightly coupled with background evolution; for the first time, we establish how this evolution modifies the Boltzmann hierarchy equations (BHEs), and (ii) resonant $ν$SI dominates the dynamics with negligible background evolution, relevant for mediator masses $\sim 10^{-6}-1$ MeV. In region (i), before matter-radiation equality, neutrino free-streaming is determined by the effective four-fermion interaction, known as the heavy-mediator limit (HML); we explore the impact of background evolution on this scenario, and from our modified BHEs, we show that self-interacting dark radiation scenarios require larger couplings than previously estimated to mimic $ν$SI. Region (ii) shows that the simplest realization of $ν$SI mediated by a (pseudo)scalar particle leads to an extra radiation contribution of $ΔN_{\rm eff}^{\rm CMB} \approx 0$, instead of the commonly quoted $\simeq 0.12$, at the CMB epoch. Overall, we highlight that our findings should be considered in any plausible scenario involving $ν$SI.

paper.title: Regge Dilaton Gravity from Feynman Diagrams
paper.abstract: Baratin and Freidel showed that closed Feynman diagrams in three and four Euclidean dimensions can be expressed as expectation values of observables in a Regge-type topological model \cite{baratin_hidden_2007, baratin_hidden_2007-1}. We extend their analysis to two dimensions with spherical, flat, or hyperbolic background geometry. Specifically, we show that the reduced Feynman amplitude of any closed (planar) scalar graph can be represented as an observable insertion in the partition function of either a discretized BF theory, whose gauge group is the isometry group of the background, or a homogeneous Regge discretization of linear dilaton gravity.

paper.title: Surrogate Modeling and Reduced-Order Methods in Gravitational-Wave Physics and Numerical Relativity: From Spectral Representations to Adaptive Compression
paper.abstract: The rapid expansion of gravitational-wave astronomy and high-precision numerical relativity has created an acute computational bottleneck: direct numerical integration of the Einstein field equations and high-dimensional Bayesian parameter estimation require millions of waveform evaluations that cannot be sustained by traditional solvers alone. Reduced-order modeling (ROM) and surrogate techniques have emerged as foundational tools to bridge this gap, compressing high-fidelity solution manifolds into compact, rapidly evaluable representations without sacrificing physical accuracy. This perspective reviews the mathematical pillars of projection-based reduced-order modeling---including Proper Orthogonal Decomposition, greedy basis selection, and the Empirical Interpolation Method---and traces their operational impact in gravitational-wave data analysis through surrogate waveform families and Reduced-Order Quadratures. We then examine the fundamental approximation barriers posed by slow Kolmogorov n-width decay in non-stationary, transient, and strongly nonlinear regimes, showing how adaptive hp-greedy domain partitioning and multi-scale spectral compression overcome these limits. Finally, we discuss how combining certified reduced-order structures with modern scientific machine learning and sensitivity-aware quantization provides a rigorous blueprint for next-generation detectors such as LISA, Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer.

paper.title: Infrared spectrum of the Type Iax supernova remnant Pa30
paper.abstract: The central star of Pa30 and its nebulosity offer one of the best opportunities to study a SN Iax explosion and its remnant. Pa30 is thought to be the product of the historical supernova explosion of 1181. No infrared spectroscopy of its extremely hot central star has hitherto been reported. Here, we present a 0.75-5 $μ$m spectrum taken by the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), together with ground-based infrared spectra, at higher resolution, covering the 0.8-2.5 $μ$m region. The spectra contain very broad lines, which we have attempted to identify and model using the codes CMFGEN and CLOUDY. The CMFGEN modelling suggests that most of the lines are due to OVI. However, CLOUDY modelling, using expected theoretical abundances for the bound remnants of SN Iax explosions, provides evidence for the presence of coronal lines of Si, S, Mg, and Al arising from a shocked gas. This strengthens the suggestion that Pa30 is indeed the remnant of a SN Iax explosion.

paper.title: Holography at finite resolution: zero-point length in AdS/CFT
paper.abstract: We explore the zero-point length $l_0$ of T-duality-inspired effective field theory in holography, distinguishing two readings. As a boundary resolution scale, $l_0$ filters the source of a bulk scalar in anti-de Sitter space and yields an exactly solvable boundary response that is ultraviolet finite without a hard cutoff and inherits the power-law tails of the zero-point-length kernel. We show that this filter is the source-normalized bulk-to-boundary transfer function of a $ν=1$ scalar evaluated at radial depth $z=l_0$. Anchoring Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces on the same radial surface gives finite entanglement entropies that retain the perimeter law and the universal sphere free energy. For two intervals in AdS$_3$, the prescription yields the mutual-information connectivity transition in closed form for arbitrary interval lengths; equal intervals maximize the connectivity window at fixed total length, and in the subresolution regime the critical separation exhibits a universal scaling law with a rescaled mutual information collapsing onto a piecewise-linear profile. As an AdS-invariant bulk proper length, $l_0$ renders the one-loop tadpole finite while preserving the conformal form of boundary two-point functions. Its exact Källén-Lehmann decomposition, however, has negative continuum weight beginning at threshold, obstructing a unitary interpretation of this propagator. The ratio $L/l_0$ identifies a crossover scale of the form factor rather than a derived spectrum of a unitary completion.

paper.title: Asteroseismology of AI Velorum: a prototype of high-amplitude delta Scuti stars
paper.abstract: AI Velorum is exceptional among high-amplitude δScuti (HADS) stars because of its multimode pulsations. Despite being an excellent target for asteroseismology, this prototype star has not been studied in detail.   We determine the stellar parameters, age, and evolutionary stage of AI Vel, constrain envelope convection and convective core overshooting, and test three opacity data sets: OPAL, OP, and OPLIB.   We analysed TESS photometry, ground-based Strömgren photometry, and HARPS spectroscopy. Modes were identified using photometric and spectroscopic methods, and empirical values of the non-adiabatic f-parameter were derived for both radial modes. Seismic modelling was performed within a Bayesian framework supported by Monte Carlo simulations.   We confirm the radial nature of the two dominant modes and identify one non-radial mode as most likely an axisymmetric dipole or quadrupole mode. Within the explored parameter space, only OPAL models reproduce the observed position of AI Vel in the HR diagram, whereas OP and OPLIB models are too cool and underluminous. All seismic models favour inefficient envelope convection (mixing-length parameter alpha_{mlt}\lesssim 0.5). Including the non-radial mode substantially reduces the formal posterior uncertainties, but the ambiguity in its identification introduces additional model-dependent uncertainties. AI Vel is an evolved, slowly rotating star in the hydrogen shell-burning phase.   Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combining pulsation frequencies with empirical f-parameters. The preference for OPAL opacities is consistent with results for several other HADS and SX Phoenicis stars but does not imply a general superiority of OPAL opacities.

paper.title: Deconstructing the cosmic baryon distribution with fast radio bursts
paper.abstract: The precise distribution of baryons in the Universe remains an open question in cosmology, as their highly diffuse nature hinders direct observation. However, mapping it is integral for precision cosmology in studies of gravitational lensing, galaxy evolution and the cosmic microwave background with current and upcoming surveys. We use fast radio bursts (FRBs) and their dispersion measures (DMs) to probe and localise this baryon distribution in the large-scale structure (LSS). Using IllustrisTNG simulations, we classify the LSS into eight bins of increasing matter density, analogous to voids, filaments, and haloes. We model the DM contribution from each substructure and compare it with the simulated DMs to infer the density estimator, the ratio of electron number to total matter density. The resulting overdetermined system is solved in a Bayesian framework with a simulation-physics-informed model. To demonstrate observational applicability, we create a Euclid-like mock galaxy catalogue and build a density estimator based on luminous matter along FRB sightlines. We apply a bias correction for the underlying dark matter distribution and compare the two density estimators to recover the electron number density across the eight bins. Electrons are predominantly localised in low-density regions, while the ensemble mean across all bins aligns with the global theoretical estimate. Combining the FRB and galaxy density estimators, we recover the density of ionised baryons as $Ω_b f_{ion} = 0.0455^{+0.0028}_{-0.0026}$ (simulation: 0.0462), corresponding to $Ω_b = 0.0479^{+0.0029}_{-0.0027}$ for $f_{ion}=0.95$. Our bin-wise electron density estimate reproduces the simulation ground truth to within 10 per cent and gives gas fractions of $0.186 \pm 0.012$, $0.179 \pm 0.015$ and $0.046 \pm 0.014$ in voids, filaments and haloes, against ground truths of 0.167, 0.173 and 0.067.

paper.title: Rotating black hole thermodynamics at NNLO in higher-curvature gravity
paper.abstract: We investigate higher-curvature corrections to black-hole thermodynamics in quasitopological gravity using perturbative Euclidean-action methods. Static, spherically symmetric black holes provide a benchmark for the action expansion, while our main application concerns five-dimensional, asymptotically flat, rotating black holes with equal angular momenta. For Einstein gravity supplemented by Gauss--Bonnet and cubic quasitopological interactions, we compute the Gibbs free energy through next-to-next-to-leading order, retaining both quadratic and cubic corrections. The result retains the full dependence on the background spin parameter, without a slow-rotation expansion, and extends to arbitrary couplings of quadratic and cubic curvature invariants. We derive the corrected mass, entropy and angular momenta, and show how rotation affects the size and sign of the corrections.

paper.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
paper.abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

paper.title: Efficient search for microlensed gravitational-wave signals with matched filtering and a two-image statistic
paper.abstract: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences can be microlensed by compact objects along the line of sight, producing frequency-dependent waveform distortions. As standard matched-filter searches rely on unlensed templates without accounting for lensing effects, microlensed signals can lose signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) through template mismatch and suffer further losses from signal-consistency tests. We quantify both effects for the $\texttt{PyCBC}$ search using microlensed injections in simulated data. The two losses occupy different regions of lens parameter space in the geometric optics representation: template mismatch is governed by the relative magnification of the two images, while the consistency-test penalty is governed by their time delay. We show that a microlensed signal lies in the two-dimensional subspace spanned by a template and its time-shifted copy, allowing the relative magnification and Morse phase to be maximized over analytically, leaving only the time delay to search. The resulting statistic requires no extension of the template bank and reduces the median loss in re-weighted SNR from $10\%$ to $1.6\%$, and the $90^\mathrm{th}$ percentile from $41\%$ to $9\%$. At a false-alarm rate of one per day, the relative detection volume improves by about $6\%$ across all injections, and by a factor of $1.9$ for the $10\%$ of injections most affected by lensing. In addition to increased detection capacities, we also show how the detection statistic can be used to establish the lensed nature of the trigger. Therefore, the work proposed here lays the foundation for an effective search and identification of microlensed signals in gravitational-wave data.

paper.title: New Observational Insights into Generalised Axion-Like Dark Energy
paper.abstract: We consider a quintessence model based on a generalised axion-like scalar field potential, originally introduced as a phenomenological framework to describe the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe. The model exhibits a tracking regime that alleviates the coincidence problem and naturally leads to a phase of late-time acceleration driven by an effective cosmological constant, without requiring fine-tuning of the scalar field initial conditions. In this work, we confront the background cosmological evolution of this model with current observations by performing a parameter inference analysis using cosmic microwave background distance priors, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, Type Ia supernovae, the SH0ES distance ladder, cosmic chronometers, and gamma-ray bursts. This analysis allows us to assess the observational viability of the model, its ability to reconcile different cosmological datasets, and its statistical performance relative to $Λ$CDM.

summary.context_outlook: 在轴子类暗能量研究中，[[Kamionkowski+ 2014]] 曾由弦论 axiverse 提出轴子暗能量；本文所采用的广义轴子势由 [[Boiza & Bouhmadi-López 2025]] 引入，并已在 [[Chiang+ 2025]]、[[Bouhmadi-López+ 2025]] 中做过初步背景约束。本文新增 CC+GRB+Pan 晚期数据组合，并与 CMB+BAO 进行联合推断和多判据比较，发现标量场额外自由度对拟合无显著提升，且不能缓解 CMB+BAO 与 PPS 之间的 Hubble 张力；不过 tracking 相在物质主导时期提供了较 ΛCDM 更丰富的早期动力学。未来可从更复杂的早期物理现象（如 [[Calderon & Linder 2026]] 讨论的位移对称修改引力视角）出发，在完整扰动层面对该类模型继续检验。

paper.title: Map-Level Inference of Primordial Gravitational Waves from the CMB with Spherical Neural Networks
paper.abstract: We train a spherical graph convolutional network to infer the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ directly from multifrequency cosmic microwave background (CMB) $B$-mode maps on the cut sky. We test the network on simulations of a generic ground-based experiment including lensed CMB, inhomogeneous noise, and stochastic Galactic dust and synchrotron emission. We compare the network with a multifrequency bandpower likelihood built from the same 20,000 simulations used to train it. Working directly on the maps, with no power-spectrum estimation or component separation, the network reduces the root-mean-square error on $r$ by a factor of 1.3 and gives well-calibrated 68% intervals 1.2 times narrower than the likelihood with the same prior. Saliency maps show that the network learns to favor the deepest regions of the sky and the cleanest frequency channels without being given the survey depth. Both approaches are tied to the foreground model they are built on: the network generalizes to some alternative foreground models without retraining, but not to a three-dimensional dust model with line-of-sight variations. The network can be extended to marginalize over foreground models by training on a broad family, making direct map-level neural inference a promising route to $r$ for future $B$-mode analyses.

summary.title_zh: 用球面神经网络从宇宙微波背景实现原初引力波的图级推断
summary.tldr: 该研究训练球面图卷积网络，直接在切割天区的多频 CMB B 模图上推断张标比 r，在含透镜效应、非均匀噪声与银河尘埃/同步辐射的模拟中，其 r 的均方根误差比多频带功率似然降低约 1.3 倍，68% 区间窄约 1.2 倍且标定良好，并能学习偏好天区最深与最干净频段，但尚未泛化到含视线变化的三维尘埃模型。
